- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overestimating recovery.
- If recent 3–5 day price drop is followed by forecast spike, apply “overshoot correction” — reduce peak forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7) and forecast deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, revert to mean reversion logic — forecast should align with 14-day MA ± 2%.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day to reflect downward momentum.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.3 or higher), forecast should be slightly higher than 14-day MA, but not exceed 10% above.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed, avoid sharp directional forecasts — use 1–2% smoothing around recent 7-day average to reduce noise.
